title: Document Data Extractor
what: A Python script that reads a text document (an exported invoice, a delivery note, a long email, a contract) and pulls out the structured data you ask for: issuer, date, amounts, line items, references. It uses the Anthropic API with a forced schema, so the output is always a JSON with the same fields, and every piece of data comes with the literal excerpt from the document it was pulled from, so you can verify it without rereading the whole document. Fields that don't appear in the document come back as null, never invented.
forWho: For anyone who keys data from documents by hand into a spreadsheet or system: administration, accounting, logistics. It pays off from a daily chunk of manual keying; with dozens of documents a day it's transformative.
capabilities: Extracts the fields you define from any text document, with a schema guaranteed by the API
Returns the literal document quote each value was pulled from, alongside every field, for quick verification
Returns null for fields the document doesn't have: filling in by guesswork is forbidden
Validates the extraction after the call (date format, numbers) and downgrades to null anything that doesn't check out, warning via stderr
Processes a single file or an entire folder, generating one JSON per document
limits: Doesn't read PDF or images directly: it works on plain text; convert first (pdftotext, copy-paste, OCR) or request the PDF-capable version as an extension
Doesn't guarantee 100%: it extracts correctly the vast majority of the time, but the pipeline must assume errors; that's why the quotes and verification exist
Shouldn't be the only control on data that moves money: an extracted amount is checked against its quote before being booked
Doesn't keep memory across documents: each one is processed in isolation

README.md
files.content:
# Document Data Extractor

Pulls structured data (issuer, date, number, amounts, line items) from text documents, with a literal quote for every value and mandatory `null` when the data isn't there.

## Installation

```bash
pip install anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"
```

## Usage

```bash
# One document, result printed to screen
python extractor.py factura.txt

# A whole folder, one JSON per document
python extractor.py --carpeta ./documentos --salida ./extraidos
```

Output per document (always the same shape):

```json
{
  "tipo_documento": "factura",
  "emisor": {"valor": "Talleres Márquez S.L.", "cita": "TALLERES MÁRQUEZ S.L."},
  "nif": {"valor": "B12345678", "cita": "CIF: B12345678"},
  "fecha": {"valor": "2025-03-14", "cita": "Fecha: 14/03/2025"},
  "numero": {"valor": "F-2025-0231", "cita": "Factura nº F-2025-0231"},
  "importe_total": {"valor": 847.0, "cita": "TOTAL: 847,00 €"},
  "conceptos": [{"descripcion": "Cambio de embrague", "importe": 700.0}],
  "_documento": "factura.txt"
}
```

## I have a PDF, not a txt

Convert it first: `pdftotext factura.pdf factura.txt` (poppler-utils package), or open the PDF and copy the text. If the PDF is a scan (image), you need OCR first; and if you want to skip the conversion, ask Claude Code to adapt the script to send the PDF directly as a document to the API.

## Adapt it to your documents

The fields live in `HERRAMIENTA` (with the `CAMPO_CON_CITA` helper) and the checks in `validar()`. Add your own: due date, IBAN, delivery address... Give each new field a concrete description: that's what improves extraction the most.

## The verification loop (don't skip it)

1. The AI extracts with a quote.
2. `validar()` checks formats in code.
3. **A person checks the value against the quote** before the data moves money.

With 20 real documents, measure: correct fields, fields that came back null when they shouldn't have, and invented fields (the serious ones). If there are any invented ones, tighten `SISTEMA` and measure again before using it for real.

setup.title: Set up the environment
setup.action: pip install anthropic (Python 3.10 or later, due to the Path | None usage).
setup.expect: python -c "import anthropic" runs with no errors.
setup.stuck: On Python 3.9, replace "Path | None" in the script with "Optional[Path]" and import Optional from typing.

setup.title: Export your key
setup.action: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." with the key created at console.anthropic.com.

setup.title: Save the script and get a test .txt
setup.action: Copy extractor.py into your working folder. Convert a real invoice: pdftotext factura.pdf factura.txt, or copy the text by hand.
setup.expect: A factura.txt file readable with cat.

setup.title: First extraction
setup.expect: The JSON with the fields filled in, each with its quote, and null wherever the invoice doesn't say.
setup.stuck: If half the document comes back null, check the .txt: PDF conversions sometimes mangle tables; try pdftotext -layout.

setup.title: Adjust the fields to your documents
setup.action: Edit HERRAMIENTA to add or remove fields (due date, IBAN...) and add its check in validar() if it has a fixed format.
setup.expect: The JSON has exactly the fields your process needs.

setup.title: Process in batch and verify
setup.action: python extractor.py --carpeta ./documentos --salida ./extraidos with 10-20 real documents, and check value against quote in each one.
setup.expect: A real accuracy measurement and zero invented fields. Only then connect it to your spreadsheet or system.

test.name: Normal run
test.input: An invoice converted to text with a clear issuer, date, number, and total.
test.expect: All fields with a value and a correct literal quote; line items with their amounts.

test.name: Incomplete document
test.input: A delivery note with no amounts.
test.expect: tipo_documento albaran, importe_total with valor null and cita null, no invented amounts.

test.name: Odd date
test.expect: Either the correctly normalized date 2025-03-14 with its quote, or null with a WARNING via stderr; never a different, invented date.

test.name: Batch with one empty file
test.input: A folder with 3 documents, one of them empty.
test.expect: It processes the 2 good ones, warns about the empty one via stderr, and exits with code 1 due to the incomplete one.

credentials.name: Anthropic API
credentials.how: Key in the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, never in the script or the repo.
credentials.cost: Pay per token; extracting a normal document with claude-haiku-4-5 costs a fraction of a cent

risks: A wrongly extracted amount that ends up booked. Mitigation: value-vs-quote checking by a person is part of the pipeline, not a nicety; for payments, double-check.
Documents with personal or tax data traveling to the API. Mitigation: check your account's retention policy and don't process what your regulations don't allow to leave the premises.
Growing confidence and shrinking verification over time. Mitigation: keep a fixed sampling rate (e.g. verify 1 in 10) forever, and everything if it moves money.
PDF-to-text conversions that mangle tables and throw off amounts. Mitigation: try pdftotext -layout and validate the total against the sum of line items in your code or spreadsheet.

examples.name: Extend with Claude Code
examples.prompt: Starting from extractor.py, add a final CSV dump with one row per document (emisor, fecha, numero, importe_total) and a warning column when any field is null.
